# TinyPrune

> TinyPrune is an open-source, local-first macOS app for automatic file cleanup using lifecycle rules, not a generic Mac cleaner. Give downloads, screenshots, installers and developer folders an expiry date, preview matches, and move expired items to macOS Trash.

## Product facts

- Released app: macOS 14 or later, Intel and Apple silicon. No Windows or Linux build is released; the Rust cross-platform implementation is unreleased development.
- Price: free, open source under the MIT license; no subscription.
- Normal cleanup moves files to Trash, never permanent deletion.
- Keep takes precedence over other rules and protects folders containing kept items. Keep matches by item identity and falls back to the recorded path.
- Preview evaluates matching and scheduling without moving items to Trash.
- Rules can use filename or folder patterns, age, and project inactivity. Developer templates support dependency and build folders such as node_modules.
- Rules can target disposable scratch projects, worktrees, virtual environments, build folders and debug logs left by coding agents. TinyPrune does not detect which tool created a file and does not manage Git worktree metadata. Review uncommitted work separately before cleaning worktree folders.
- Core cleanup requires no account or network access and reads filesystem metadata, not file contents. Key-enabled direct-download builds, including ad-hoc builds without an Apple account, use EdDSA-authenticated Sparkle updates over HTTPS. Checks follow Check for new versions (default on); installation is user-confirmed through Update Now/the native dialog, never automatic. Homebrew never constructs Sparkle; Homebrew/no-key copies use GitHub release notices and manual download or brew upgrade. First-install Gatekeeper approval is unchanged; non-quarantined Sparkle replacements are expected, not end-to-end verified.
- Interfaces include the native app, Finder menu and tinyprune CLI with JSON output and configuration validate, preview, apply and export commands.
- Current early releases are not Developer ID signed or notarized. Install with `brew install --cask navig-me/tap/tinyprune` or download the DMG from GitHub Releases; consult Releases for the current version and signing details. The landing-page playground uses sample files and simulated time; it never touches real files.
- The app has no telemetry. Website analytics are separate: the tinyprune.com marketing website loads Google Analytics and PostHog.
- Recovery depends on the item remaining in Trash and Finder offering Put Back; TinyPrune does not restore items and is not a backup. Trash may be emptied by you or macOS.
